People connect their own YouTube accounts.

## OAuth client for apps

The Gateway holds the OAuth client; the app runs the sign-in itself and keeps people's tokens.

- **Make the OAuth app here:** [console.cloud.google.com](https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/credentials)
- **Settings:** `YOUTUBE_CLIENT_ID`, `YOUTUBE_CLIENT_SECRET`
- **Built in:** nothing to add, only the client to set

### Redirect URI

Register each app's own callback at the provider:

```text
https://<app>.<your app domain>/integrations/social/youtube
https://<app>.<your app domain>/integrations/social/gmb
```

`<app>.<your app domain>` is the app's address, like `crm.apps.example.com`.

### Make the OAuth app

1. Open [console.cloud.google.com](https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/credentials) and create an OAuth app (sometimes called a client or an integration).
2. Add the redirect URI above.
3. Copy the client ID and the client secret. The secret is often shown once.

Steps for this provider are brief. [Open an issue](https://github.com/every-app/every-app/issues/new?template=provider-request.yml&title=Provider%20guide%3A%20YouTube) to request a full guide.

### Set it on your Gateway

From your EveryApp folder:

```bash
pnpm everyapp secret set YOUTUBE_CLIENT_ID YOUTUBE_CLIENT_SECRET
```

Each value goes in at a hidden prompt. Or, as an owner or admin, paste the client in **Manage workspace → Providers → Add OAuth provider**.

### Use it in an app

```ts
capabilities: {
  youtube: { access: "read", why: "What the app does with it." },
},
```

### Check it worked

- `pnpm everyapp provider show youtube` shows the client as set, and the redirect URI.
